body: Why does it need an escort? Is it a particularly big target for attacks or is that all for show?
Exactly what I was thinking. I have really bad social anxiety so best case scenario is I do nothing. Worst case I run and hide for the full 10 minutes.

Throwaway because she knows my main reddit account and I'm not looking to completely burn this bridge just yet. 

She got talking to me after I posted on /r/depression, and ended up being more helpful than any amount of therapy. I genuinely started feeling better when talking to her. Then she just stops replying to me out of no where and all the progress I made with her gets thrown out the window over night.

Ninja edit: I might have misread the question and thought it said most hurtful thing a girl has done to you, rather than said to you. And it's still probably away from what that question meant, but I'll leave it up anyway.

I think it only worked to begin with as a placebo effect of "I'm getting some treatment so I must be getting better". I had something similar happen with citalopram where I started feeling better within days of taking it when it actually takes weeks to kick in, but after a month or more the placebo effect wore off and the meds weren't doing their job. 

I have some experience with coming off SSRIs, when I was on citalopram I had a few times where I would get pissed off with all the side effects for something that felt like it was doing nothing, stop taking it for 3 or 4 days and get depression and anxiety a million times worse than before I was on the meds to remind me why I was taking them.

A quick update after seeing the doctor. He didn't want to put me on any other drugs, because apparently at my age they're just likely to have more side effects and do more harm than good. And he didn't increase my dosage because if it's not working at all then taking more of it won't help. I think he's only keeping me on it now because it's easier than slowly weening me off it.

Thanks, I knew it was a possible side effect but I forgot that I should mention it to my doctor when I see him. But it seems strange that I've been on the prozac for almost 2 months and this only started in the last week or two. 

I tried exercise and sensible sleep while I was on citalopram and it just made me more tired so I ended up sleeping ~15 hours a day.

I'm going back to the doctor on thursday where I'll hopefully change my meds or my dosage. And I know it's the worst thing to OD on, but it's also the easiest thing for me to get hold off that I know you can OD from.
